page.layout: One page of verse in one column; page number at top right; gathering signature at foot.

p.i: Autumnus amplo pallidus ubere Irages colonis fuderit, & suos Pomona fructus legerit, heu, rigens Tristi recurret Bruma vice. Heu, nives Per arua densa, Sarmatico & gelu Astricta passim flumina nos focum Seruare cogent. Linque domum & libros, Quid inquieta sollicitudine Mentem fatigas semper, & hostium Horrescis astus multiplices? Licet Quandoque Musa decutere anxia Seueriorum tadia frontibus: Atque aegra curis pectora edacibus Leuare honestis risibus, & locis, Quos casta Pallas, quos Citharaparens Phoebus sonora diligat, & Pudor. At quaeris hortus quo sit us est loco Quoque urbe distat passibus. An via Longinqua tardo fit nimium seni? Et quae sit illi forma? Loquaciter Haec cuncta dicet Musa. Palatij Vicina plani prata videt, suum Quà mane Titan igniuomus diem Terris redonat: Quà medios micat Emensus axes lucidior, potest Torrentis Arua cernere concitos Cursus, & undis turbidam arenulis Ripam. Volucris sed Rhodani placens Audire gaudet murmur, equus vagas

page.notes: The printed page number is set at the top right and reads 185. The ampersand-like sign is printed as "&". Several words in the italic verse are uncertain at line ends, notably "Irages", "Horrescis" and "sit us est", and are given as printed without marks because the scan is only partly legible.
